prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1465; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
On arrival at the intersection in Pasadena, Texas, I found a side-impact collision between two passenger vehicles. Driver 1 was operating a sedan that had entered the intersection when Driver 2's vehicle struck its driver's side. Driver 1 is the individual listed on the policy for the sedan. A Passenger was seated in the vehicle at the time.

Driver 1 reported pain in the right shoulder. The nature of the impact, with the force directed into the side of the cab, is consistent with the injury described. Driver 2 stated that the collision happened as Driver 1 described it, and two independent witnesses gave accounts that agree with both drivers' versions. Scene photographs show damage concentrated on the driver's side of Driver 1's vehicle and on the front quarter of Driver 2's vehicle, which fits the reported angle of impact.

I found no indication of prior damage to either vehicle. It was not fully clear from the scene where in the vehicle Driver 1 was seated at the moment of impact, and this will need to be confirmed in follow-up interviews. Both vehicles were towed from the scene.
